subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The probability a bus is late is 0.15. What is the probability it is not late?
Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.25 and P(B) = 0.45. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events P(A or B) = 0.25 + 0.45 = 0.7.

questions.q: In a Venn diagram of 30 students, 12 study French only, 9 study Spanish only and 4 study both. How many study neither?
questions.explain: 30 − (12 + 9 + 4) = 5 students study neither.

questions.q: Two classes have the same mean test score, but class A has a larger range. What does this suggest?
options: Class A scores are more spread out
Class A scored higher on average
questions.explain: A larger range indicates the data is more spread out (more variable).

questions.q: In a tree diagram, the first branch shows P = 0.6 and a following branch shows P = 0.5. What is the probability of both happening?
questions.explain: Multiply along the branches: 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.3.

questions.q: In a frequency table, value 2 occurs 3 times, value 5 occurs 4 times and value 8 occurs 1 time. How many data values are there in total?
questions.explain: Total number of values = sum of the frequencies = 3 + 4 + 1 = 8.

questions.q: To estimate the mean of grouped data you multiply each class frequency by the class:
questions.explain: Estimated mean uses the mid-point of each class multiplied by its frequency.

questions.q: On the probability scale, what value represents an impossible event?
questions.explain: An impossible event has probability 0.

questions.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.3. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.q: A survey only asks people leaving a gym about exercise habits. This sample is:
questions.explain: Only gym-goers are sampled, so the sample is biased toward active people.

questions.q: A spinner has 8 equal sectors numbered 1 to 8. What is P(spinning an even number)?
questions.explain: There are 4 even numbers out of 8, so 4/8 = 1/2.

questions.q: A bag has 4 red, 3 green and 1 yellow ball. What is P(green)?
questions.explain: 3 green out of 8 total gives 3/8.

questions.q: As temperature rises, sales of hot soup fall. This shows:
questions.explain: One increasing while the other decreases is negative correlation.

questions.q: For grouped data with classes 0-20, 20-40, 40-60 and frequencies 7, 11, 3, which is the modal class?
questions.explain: The class with the highest frequency (11) is 20-40.

questions.q: Two fair coins are flipped. What is P(both heads)?
questions.explain: P(H) × P(H) = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4 for independent events.

questions.q: A coin is flipped 200 times and lands heads 90 times. What is the experimental probability of heads?
questions.explain: Relative frequency = 90 ÷ 200 = 0.45.

questions.q: A pictogram uses one symbol = 10 books. How many books do 3.5 symbols represent?
On the probability scale, what value represents a certain event?
questions.explain: A certain event has probability 1.

questions.q: How many outcomes are in the sample space when rolling two fair six-sided dice?
questions.explain: 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes.

questions.q: The probability it rains is 0.3. What is the probability it does not rain?
In a frequency table, the value 3 occurs 5 times and the value 4 occurs 2 times. What is the mode?
questions.explain: The value with the highest frequency is 3 (occurring 5 times).

questions.q: To find an estimate of the mean from grouped data, you divide the total of (mid-point × frequency) by:
questions.explain: Estimated mean = sum of (mid-point × frequency) ÷ total frequency.
